    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count

Armored Likho Still Sync gRPC C2 beacon (tg4service.com / still.rpc.Sync) AICommand & Control High
Hunts Still Sync's Rust stealer beaconing to its gRPC-over-HTTPS C2 at tg4service[.]com:443 using the article-specific /still.rpc.Sync/ service paths (RegisterMachine, GetMachineSettings, CheckFiles). These URI paths and the FlatBuffers/gRPC POST shape are unique to this implant. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact gRPC service paths (/still.rpc.Sync/RegisterMachine|GetMachineSettings|CheckFiles) and C2 host tg4service[.]com / 159.198.37.74 — these strings are unique to the Still Sync implant and won't collide with benign traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/armored-likho-targets-government.html • https://gbhackers.com/likho-hijacks-microphones/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal gRPC microservices that coincidentally use a 'rpc.Sync' service name (unlikely to hit the full still.rpc.Sync path)
  • Security researchers/sandboxes replaying the sample and generating the same beacons
  • Proxy category miscategorization if the domain gets sinkholed and points to a benign IP
  • Threat-intel scanners resolving tg4service.com for enrichment
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: On the alerting host pivot to InitiatingProcessSHA256 and check for a Rust/Tauri-signed or unsigned binary spawning the connection; compare hash to the IOC set (c1d1ee16..., 6280...). 2) Contain: Network-isolate the device via Defender, block tg4service[.]com and 159.198.37.74 at proxy/firewall, and suspend the associated Telegram session server-side if account theft is suspected. 3) Hunt: Search the org for the same SHA256, for the sibling C2 domains (srwinservice.com, screenserv.com, windowserv.net), and for a 'TReload' service or hidden 'bin' file dropped alongside the executable.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "tg4service.com"
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("still.rpc.Sync/RegisterMachine","still.rpc.Sync/GetMachineSettings","still.rpc.Sync/CheckFiles")
   or RemoteIP == "159.198.37.74"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationHostName has "tg4service.com"
   or RequestURL has_any ("still.rpc.Sync/RegisterMachine","still.rpc.Sync/GetMachineSettings","still.rpc.Sync/CheckFiles")
   or DestinationIP == "159.198.37.74"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Armored Likho Tauri donation-app dropper C2 (orderapiserver.info catalog endpoints) AIDelivery High
Hunts the fake donation-service dropper fetching its decoy catalog from orderapiserver[.]info via the /public/categories and /public/products endpoints while it decrypts and launches the Still Toolkit in the background. Anchored on the article's exact staging host and REST paths. Rationale: Uses the article's exact staging host orderapiserver[.]info (187.127.153.38) and its /public/categories and /public/products REST paths — the decoy-catalog endpoints the Rust/Tauri dropper hits, which are campaign-specific and not part of any legitimate donation service seen in the org. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/ • https://hackread.com/armored-likho-government-energy-busysnake-stealer/
ATT&CKT1608.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A genuine fundraising/e-commerce site that happens to expose /public/categories and /public/products (mitigated by pinning the exact orderapiserver.info host)
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling resolving/fetching the IOC domain
  • Sandbox detonation of the sample generating the same catalog requests
  • Web crawlers/link-preview bots touching the domain
Response runbook
1) Triage: Identify InitiatingProcessFileName/SHA256 making the request — expect an unfamiliar Rust/Tauri app posing as a Russian foundation donation tool; check its folder path and signature. 2) Contain: Isolate the host, block orderapiserver[.]info and 187.127.153.38, and quarantine the dropper binary. 3) Hunt: On that host look for a subsequently-launched Still Sync/Still Audio payload, a TReload service, tdata access, and outbound tg4service[.]com beacons; sweep the fleet for the same dropper hash and download source.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "orderapiserver.info" or RemoteIP == "187.127.153.38"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/public/categories","/public/products") or RemoteUrl has "orderapiserver.info"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationHostName has "orderapiserver.info" or DestinationIP == "187.127.153.38"
   or RequestURL has_any ("orderapiserver.info/public/categories","orderapiserver.info/public/products")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Still Sync TReload service persistence + implant CLI flags (--firefly/--console) AIInstallation High
Hunts Still Sync establishing persistence by creating a 'TReload' Windows service and/or launching with its distinctive command-line flags (--firefly, --console, --db) and STILL_* environment configuration. These service and flag strings are unique to the implant. Rationale: Pins the implant's own service name 'TReload' (created when --console is absent) plus its unique CLI flags (--firefly trace thread) and STILL_SYNC_ADDR/STILL_SEND_PATH/STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE env-var config strings — all verbatim from the article and effectively zero-collision in a normal enterprise. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Services
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate third-party product coincidentally installing a service literally named 'TReload' (rare; validate ServiceFileName path)
  • Developer debugging setting env vars with a 'STILL_' prefix for an unrelated project
  • Security testing/red-team replaying the toolkit in a lab
  • EDR/telemetry sample-analysis VM detonating the binary
Response runbook
1) Triage: Inspect the ServiceFileName / process folder path and hash; a service named TReload pointing at an AppData or user-writable path plus STILL_* flags is high-confidence malicious. 2) Contain: Stop and delete the TReload service, isolate the host, and quarantine the binary and the hidden 'bin' trace file in the same folder. 3) Hunt: Confirm outbound tg4service[.]com traffic, check for tdata access and Telegram session theft, and sweep other hosts for the same service name, CLI flags, and IOC hashes.
union
(DeviceEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where ActionType == "ServiceInstalled"
 | where AdditionalFields has "TReload" or RegistryValueData has "TReload"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ActionType, ReportedField=tostring(AdditionalFields), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--firefly","STILL_SYNC_ADDR","STILL_SEND_PATH","STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE")
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ActionType="ProcessCreate", ReportedField=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where EventID in (7045, 4697)
 | where ServiceName has "TReload" or ServiceFileName has "TReload"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, EventID, ServiceName, ServiceFileName),
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where EventID == 4688
 | where CommandLine has_any ("--firefly","STILL_SYNC_ADDR","STILL_SEND_PATH","STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE")
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, EventID, NewProcessName, CommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Still Sync Implant CLI Flags and STILL Environment Config
id: 4a9c2f18-5d61-4b7e-a2c9-8f1e3d6b0c74
description: Detects Still Sync launching with its distinctive command-line flags or STILL_* configuration strings
references:
  - https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/18
tags:
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1564.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--firefly'
      - 'STILL_SYNC_ADDR'
      - 'STILL_SEND_PATH'
      - 'STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @CommandLine:(*--firefly* OR *STILL_SYNC_ADDR* OR *STILL_SEND_PATH* OR *STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/(--firefly|STILL_SYNC_ADDR|STILL_SEND_PATH|STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*--firefly*" OR Processes.process="*--console*" OR Processes.process="*STILL_SYNC_ADDR*" OR Processes.process="*STILL_SEND_PATH*" OR Processes.process="*STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*--firefly*" OR Processes.process="*--console*" OR Processes.process="*STILL_SYNC_ADDR*" OR Processes.process="*STILL_SEND_PATH*" OR Processes.process="*STILL_TELEGRAM_PASSCODE*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Still Sync Telegram tdata theft via non-Telegram process + SeBackupPrivilege abuse AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts a non-Telegram process reading the Telegram Desktop 'tdata' session directory (standard, Microsoft Store 'TelegramMessenge' package, or via C:\ extended scan) — the core session-stealing behaviour of Still Sync, including its FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS / SeBackupPrivilege fallback to grab locked session files. Rationale: Targets the article's exact session-theft target paths (\Telegram Desktop\tdata, the Microsoft Store 'TelegramMessenge' LocalCache\Roaming location) accessed by a process other than Telegram.exe — the defining Still Sync behaviour. FileCount>=3 in 10m separates a stealer copying the session from an incidental single-file touch. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/ • https://gbhackers.com/likho-hijacks-microphones/
ATT&CKT1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup software (Veeam, Acronis, Windows File History) enumerating user AppData including tdata
  • Antivirus/EDR on-demand scans reading tdata files
  • Telegram helper/updater processes not named Telegram.exe
  • Sync/cloud tools (OneDrive/Dropbox) if a user redirects Telegram data
  • Forensic/DFIR collection tools imaging the profile
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("veeam.backup.shell.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SenseCncProxy.exe","OneDrive.exe","Backup.exe","Acronis.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Identify InitiatingProcessFileName/SHA256 touching tdata and confirm it is not a backup/AV product; a Rust/Tauri binary from user-writable path reading many tdata files is high-confidence Still Sync. 2) Contain: Isolate the host, quarantine the binary, and treat the affected Telegram account as compromised — terminate all active Telegram sessions and force re-auth/2FA. 3) Hunt: Look for the follow-on tg4service[.]com upload, SeBackupPrivilege / FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS use, VSS/CheckFiles activity, and the same process touching tdata across other hosts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata" or (FolderPath has "tdata" and FolderPath has_any ("LocalCache\\Roaming","TelegramMessenge"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("Telegram.exe","Update.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FileCount=dcount(FileName), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 10), any(FolderPath) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where FileCount >= 3
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata" or (TargetFilePath has "tdata" and TargetFilePath has_any ("LocalCache\\Roaming","TelegramMessenge"))
| where ActingProcessName !has "Telegram.exe"
| summarize FileCount=dcount(TargetFileName), SampleFiles=make_set(TargetFileName, 10) by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where FileCount >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Telegram Process Accessing tdata Session Directory
id: 9c3e7b25-1a48-4d90-bf62-7e2c5a8d3f11
description: Detects a non-Telegram process reading the Telegram Desktop tdata session folder, as done by Still Sync
references:

detection:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\Telegram?Desktop\\tdata\\* OR *tdata*) -@Image:(*\\Telegram.exe OR *\\telegram.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo TargetFileName=/\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\Telegram\.exe$/i

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*LocalCache\\Roaming\\*tdata*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search process_name!="Telegram.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Armored Likho Still Toolkit C2 infrastructure IOC match (domains + IPs) AICommand & Control Medium
Broad network sweep matching any host communicating with the Still Toolkit C2/staging infrastructure named in the article's IOC table (eight domains, eight IPs). Catch-all pivot for hosts that evade the behaviour-specific rules. Rationale: Direct match on the full IOC domain/IP set from the article's infrastructure table — low-FP by construction since these are dedicated actor-controlled hosts; serves as the safety net if the behaviour-specific detections miss a variant. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/armored-likho-still-toolkit/121033/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/armored-likho-targets-government.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platforms/scanners resolving the IOC domains for enrichment
  • Shared-hosting IP reuse where a listed IP later serves benign tenants (validate domain+IP together)
  • Sandbox/lab detonation of samples
  • Researchers or blocklist-validation tooling touching the domains
Response runbook
1) Triage: Confirm the connection initiator process/hash on the matching host and correlate with the behaviour rules (dropper, tdata theft, TReload). 2) Contain: Block all eight domains and IPs at DNS/proxy/firewall, isolate any confirmed host, and rotate credentials/Telegram sessions for affected users. 3) Hunt: Expand the time window to 90 days for first-contact, pivot on any newly-registered lookalike '*serv*'/'*service*' domains on the same ASNs (149440, 22612), and check for the Still Audio eavesdropping implant on the same hosts.
let iocDomains = dynamic(["orderapiserver.info","tg4service.com","srwinservice.com","screenserv.com","windowserv.net","managementapiservice.com","service8date.com","updateservs.com"]);
let iocIPs = dynamic(["187.127.153.38","159.198.37.74","213.252.244.123","23.26.237.250","23.27.24.30","188.212.124.178","145.223.69.143","145.223.68.66"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (iocIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (iocDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let iocDomains = dynamic(["orderapiserver.info","tg4service.com","srwinservice.com","screenserv.com","windowserv.net","managementapiservice.com","service8date.com","updateservs.com"]);
let iocIPs = dynamic(["187.127.153.38","159.198.37.74","213.252.244.123","23.26.237.250","23.27.24.30","188.212.124.178","145.223.69.143","145.223.68.66"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in (iocIPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (iocDomains) or RequestURL has_any (iocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c1d1ee16b92e6a138ffa048855f75d7d17674b250d8b422a50a86c9ff207186d", "62801f6223e860a7cca271522e303b2d68f0365d2fa8c828d012d8859e52a773", "4bd7c352ae277b0e38d07beedd4dd507d4bc09fb10ea2a5dc0bcbeeda5e5afdd", "2ca8adbab98ebe305eacf272cf48f5a03ac41b097236a7723821848ae31ef141", "439255736797bc88bd19f282449e0436") or SHA1 in~ ("c1d1ee16b92e6a138ffa048855f75d7d17674b250d8b422a50a86c9ff207186d", "62801f6223e860a7cca271522e303b2d68f0365d2fa8c828d012d8859e52a773", "4bd7c352ae277b0e38d07beedd4dd507d4bc09fb10ea2a5dc0bcbeeda5e5afdd", "2ca8adbab98ebe305eacf272cf48f5a03ac41b097236a7723821848ae31ef141", "439255736797bc88bd19f282449e0436") or MD5 in~ ("c1d1ee16b92e6a138ffa048855f75d7d17674b250d8b422a50a86c9ff207186d", "62801f6223e860a7cca271522e303b2d68f0365d2fa8c828d012d8859e52a773", "4bd7c352ae277b0e38d07beedd4dd507d4bc09fb10ea2a5dc0bcbeeda5e5afdd", "2ca8adbab98ebe305eacf272cf48f5a03ac41b097236a7723821848ae31ef141", "439255736797bc88bd19f282449e0436")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c1d1ee16b92e6a138ffa048855f75d7d17674b250d8b422a50a86c9ff207186d", "62801f6223e860a7cca271522e303b2d68f0365d2fa8c828d012d8859e52a773", "4bd7c352ae277b0e38d07beedd4dd507d4bc09fb10ea2a5dc0bcbeeda5e5afdd", "2ca8adbab98ebe305eacf272cf48f5a03ac41b097236a7723821848ae31ef141", "439255736797bc88bd19f282449e0436") or SHA1 in~ ("c1d1ee16b92e6a138ffa048855f75d7d17674b250d8b422a50a86c9ff207186d", "62801f6223e860a7cca271522e303b2d68f0365d2fa8c828d012d8859e52a773", "4bd7c352ae277b0e38d07beedd4dd507d4bc09fb10ea2a5dc0bcbeeda5e5afdd", "2ca8adbab98ebe305eacf272cf48f5a03ac41b097236a7723821848ae31ef141", "439255736797bc88bd19f282449e0436") or MD5 in~ ("c1d1ee16b92e6a138ffa048855f75d7d17674b250d8b422a50a86c9ff207186d", "62801f6223e860a7cca271522e303b2d68f0365d2fa8c828d012d8859e52a773", "4bd7c352ae277b0e38d07beedd4dd507d4bc09fb10ea2a5dc0bcbeeda5e5afdd", "2ca8adbab98ebe305eacf272cf48f5a03ac41b097236a7723821848ae31ef141", "439255736797bc88bd19f282449e0436")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["c1d1ee16b92e6a138ffa048855f75d7d17674b250d8b422a50a86c9ff207186d", "62801f6223e860a7cca271522e303b2d68f0365d2fa8c828d012d8859e52a773", "4bd7c352ae277b0e38d07beedd4dd507d4bc09fb10ea2a5dc0bcbeeda5e5afdd", "2ca8adbab98ebe305eacf272cf48f5a03ac41b097236a7723821848ae31ef141", "439255736797bc88bd19f282449e0436"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hacker News
2026-08-13 7 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Threat actors have begun to exploit a newly disclosed Microsoft SharePoint vulnerability following the release of a proof-of-concept (PoC) code. The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-55040 (CVSS score: 9.1), which refers to a critical security feature bypass that stems from weak authentication. It was patched by Microsoft as part of its July 2026 Patch Tuesday updates. "The authentication

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] SharePoint STS certificate/thumbprint disclosure endpoint accessed from external IP (CVE-2026-55040 recon) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains

SharePoint STS certificate/thumbprint disclosure endpoint accessed from external IP (CVE-2026-55040 recon) AIReconnaissance High
Hunts unauthenticated access to /_layouts/15/metadata/json/1 from an external source. This endpoint leaks SharePoint's own STS signing certificate and x5t thumbprint, which the CVE-2026-55040 chain reuses to forge a valid actor token. External access to it is the first observable step of the forged-JWT auth bypass. Rationale: Uses the exact Rapid7-documented information-disclosure path (/_layouts/15/metadata/json/1) that leaks the STS x5t thumbprint the exploit reuses; scoping to external source IPs strips the legitimate internal S2S handshake traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ra-microsoft-sharepoint-jwt-token-authentication-bypass-cve-2026-55040/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/13/microsoft-sharepoint-cve-2026-55040-poc-exploit/
ATT&CKT1190 T1606.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SharePoint hybrid / Office 365 federation trust pulling STS metadata (normally from a Microsoft/internal IP)
  • Authorized vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Qualys/Tenable) probing SharePoint endpoints
  • External uptime/health monitors configured against the metadata path
  • Penetration testers running the public Rapid7 PoC during an authorized engagement
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has "HealthProbe" and csUserAgent !has "Nessus" and csUserAgent !has "Qualys"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source cIP is not a sanctioned scanner or hybrid-federation endpoint; pull the surrounding IIS requests from that cIP for /_api/web/currentuser or /_api/contextinfo hits (post-bypass). 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF/edge and confirm the SharePoint server is on the July 2026 patch level; if unpatched, restrict the endpoint and prioritize patching. 3) Hunt: pivot on the cIP across all SharePoint front-ends, review SharePoint audit logs for file access/modification under admin/site-admin identities, and search for the alg:none Authorization header (UC2).
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem =~ "/_layouts/15/metadata/json/1"
| where cIP != "127.0.0.1" and not(ipv4_is_private(cIP))
| summarize Hits=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), UserAgents=make_set(csUserAgent, 10), StatusCodes=make_set(scStatus, 10) by Computer, cIP, csUserName
| order by FirstSeen desc

SharePoint CVE-2026-55040 chain: metadata recon then post-bypass API calls from one external IP AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates the full CVE-2026-55040 walk from a single external source IP within one hour: recon on /_layouts/15/metadata/json/1 followed by post-bypass identity/state calls to /_api/web/currentuser and/or /_api/contextinfo (form-digest acquisition for state-changing operations). The sequence from an external IP indicates a successful forged-token impersonation, not scattered scanning. Rationale: Chains the three Rapid7-documented paths in attack order (metadata/json/1 recon -> currentuser identity check -> contextinfo form digest) from a single external IP inside a 1h window, which distinguishes successful impersonation from opportunistic scanning and cannot be expressed on Defender endpoint telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ra-microsoft-sharepoint-jwt-token-authentication-bypass-cve-2026-55040/ • https://securityonline.info/sharepoint-auth-bypass-cve-2026-55040/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078 T1087
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Automated vulnerability scanner walking SharePoint endpoints in sequence from a single IP
  • SharePoint hybrid federation host touching metadata plus API endpoints (typically an internal/Microsoft IP, filtered by the external-IP clause)
  • Legitimate external integration/service account that authenticates then calls contextinfo (rarely preceded by metadata/json/1 recon)
  • Bug-bounty/pentest activity from a sanctioned source IP
Suppression filter
| where UserAgents !has "Nessus" and UserAgents !has "Qualys" and UserAgents !has "HealthProbe"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the cIP is external and non-scanner; check the response codes — 200s on /_api/web/currentuser and /_api/contextinfo after the metadata hit indicate the forged token was accepted. 2) Contain: block the cIP, patch/verify the SharePoint server (July 2026 CU), and rotate/reissue the SharePoint STS certificate since its thumbprint was disclosed and abused. 3) Hunt: enumerate all state-changing operations from that IP (file writes, permission changes, user/SID enumeration), review SharePoint audit for admin-SID impersonation, and sweep other front-ends for the same three-endpoint pattern.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where csUriStem in~ ("/_layouts/15/metadata/json/1", "/_api/web/currentuser", "/_api/contextinfo")
| where cIP != "127.0.0.1" and not(ipv4_is_private(cIP))
| summarize Endpoints=make_set(csUriStem), ReqCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Statuses=make_set(scStatus, 10), UserAgents=make_set(csUserAgent, 5) by cIP, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-55040")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-55040")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Trojanized Enveil 'SecurityPDF' viewer downloaded from fake sites and dropping Troy loader (new.exe) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] FudModule SYSTEM injection: msiexec.exe spawned by services.exe running as SYSTEM · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Lazarus Exploits Windows Zero-Day to Gain SYSTEM Access and Deploy Backdoor
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Lazarus MISTPEN DLL side-load chain via trojanized PDF viewer (libmupdf.dll + recon modules)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ForestTiger/MISTPEN C2 to Enveil-impersonation domains and hijacked-infrastructure IPs · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Lazarus MISTPEN DLL side-load chain via trojanized PDF viewer (libmupdf.dll + recon modules) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Operation Dream Job DLL side-loading chain where a trojanized PDF viewer loads a malicious libmupdf.dll that in turn loads MISTPEN reconnaissance/screenshot modules (Release_GetInfoPlugin_x64.dll, Release_PvPlugin_x64.dll, OneScreenCapture64.dll) and the FudModule LPE loader (Afd4Eop12_x64.dll). Article-specific because it keys on the exact uniquely-named Lazarus modules and known loader/MISTPEN SHA256s rather than generic side-loading. Rationale: Keys on the four uniquely-named MISTPEN/FudModule module DLLs and the loader+MISTPEN SHA256s from Check Point; libmupdf.dll is excluded from name-matching (legit MuPDF/SumatraPDF library) and only caught via hash to avoid FPs.   • EDR/AV quarantine copy of the module triggering a re-scan image load
  • Internal red-team replay of Lazarus TTPs using the same module names

Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcess (the PDF viewer) full path, signer, and SHA256; confirm whether it is a masqueraded SecurityPDF.exe or a legit reader, and whether the loaded DLL SHA256 matches the CPR IOCs. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the loader process tree, and capture memory (MISTPEN/Troy run in-memory) before reboot. 3) Hunt: sweep for %TEMP%\new.exe, services.exe→msiexec.exe SYSTEM child, and outbound to envell.xyz/enveil.online/uxtramine.org across the fleet; check recent LinkedIn-themed recruiter emails to the user.

Trojanized Enveil 'SecurityPDF' viewer downloaded from fake sites and dropping Troy loader (new.exe) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the second Operation Dream Job infection path: SecurityPDF.exe downloaded from Enveil-impersonating domains (envell.xyz/enveil.online/uxtramine.org) and then dropping/executing %TEMP%\new.exe, the in-memory loader for the Troy backdoor. Article-specific via the exact binary names, download origins and SecurityPDF/Troy SHA256s. Rationale: Uses the exact trojanized-viewer name (SecurityPDF.exe), its drop target %TEMP%\new.exe, the three Enveil-impersonating download domains, and the SecurityPDF/Troy SHA256s from Check Point — all high-fidelity, none generic. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/shattering-the-dream-when-a-job-offer-becomes-a-zero-day-attack/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/12/north-korea-lazarus-fake-job-offers/
ATT&CKT1566.003 T1204.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An unrelated legitimate app that happens to write a file literally named new.exe to temp (rare; scoped by SecurityPDF.exe parent)
  • Analyst downloading the sample from a fake domain into a lab VM under EDR
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling caching the SecurityPDF binary during retro-hunt
  • Internal software named 'SecurityPDF' by coincidence (verify signer/hash before escalation)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files" and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName != "")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm SecurityPDF.exe signer and SHA256 against IOCs, and pull FileOriginUrl to see if it came from envell.xyz/enveil.online/uxtramine.org; check the user's mailbox for a recruiter lure referencing an encrypted PDF. 2) Contain: isolate host, quarantine SecurityPDF.exe and %TEMP%\new.exe, revoke the user's active sessions/tokens (Troy = interactive shell + exfil). 3) Hunt: pivot to MISTPEN module image loads (UC1), services.exe→msiexec.exe SYSTEM child (UC3), and C2 beacons (UC4); block the three domains and both hijacked-infra IPs org-wide.

FudModule SYSTEM injection: msiexec.exe spawned by services.exe running as SYSTEM AIExploitation Medium
Detects the FudModule 3.1 / AFD.sys (CVE-2026-68820) SYSTEM-level foothold where MISTPEN is injected into a msiexec.exe child of services.exe running at System integrity with no MSI install context — the anomalous host in which Smart App Control (VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState) is tampered with. This parent→child pairing does not occur during normal MSI installs (which run under svchost.exe/msiserver). Rationale: services.exe directly spawning a SYSTEM-integrity msiexec.exe with no .msi on the command line is the observable host-side artifact of FudModule injecting MISTPEN into a SYSTEM process — a parent/child pair that legitimate Windows Installer flows never produce. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/shattering-the-dream-when-a-job-offer-becomes-a-zero-day-attack/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/lazarus-hackers-exploited-windows-zero-day-to-target-defense-firms/
ATT&CKT1068 T1055.001 T1562.001 T1014
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Rare third-party service that legitimately shells out to msiexec for maintenance (verify command line and signer)
  • Enterprise software self-repair invoked by a service without a .msi argument (uncommon)
  • Endpoint management agents that re-run installers under a service context
  • Red-team AFD.sys/FudModule emulation on an authorized host
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "msiserver"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the msiexec.exe has System integrity, parent services.exe, and no .msi arg; dump its loaded modules and injected threads (look for MISTPEN) and check Smart App Control / code-integrity policy state on the host. 2) Contain: isolate the host immediately — SYSTEM is already achieved; capture RAM, then reboot to clear the in-memory rootkit and force full re-image given kernel-mode FudModule presence. 3) Hunt: confirm the AFD.sys CVE-2026-68820 August patch is applied fleet-wide via DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities; sweep for the DLL side-load chain (UC1) and C2 (UC4) on the same and peer hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "msiexec.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "services.exe"
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel =~ "System"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has ".msi"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\services.exe"
| where CommandLine !has ".msi"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType

ForestTiger/MISTPEN C2 to Enveil-impersonation domains and hijacked-infrastructure IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Detects command-and-control from Operation Dream Job to the three Enveil-impersonating domains (envell.xyz, enveil.online, uxtramine.org) and the two hijacked-infrastructure C2 IPs (135.181.67.203, 135.181.185.158). Article-specific IOC-driven network detection for MISTPEN/ForestTiger beaconing that otherwise hides in legitimate compromised WordPress/SharePoint/Roundcube traffic. Rationale: All five network IOCs (three impersonation domains + two hijacked-infrastructure IPs) are confirmed by Check Point; matching them directly is the highest-fidelity signal for MISTPEN/ForestTiger C2. The IP clause supplements DNS for hosts beaconing directly to the C2 without name resolution. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/shattering-the-dream-when-a-job-offer-becomes-a-zero-day-attack/ • https://securityaffairs.com/197098/uncategorized/north-korean-lazarus-group-uses-windows-zero-day-in-operation-dream-job.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1584.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel/EDR sandbox detonating the sample and beaconing to the C2
  • Analyst manually browsing the fake Enveil sites during investigation
  • Passive DNS / scanning tooling resolving the IOC domains for enrichment
  • Firewall already sinkholing the domains (resolution logged but connection blocked)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess making the connection — msiexec.exe/services.exe (FudModule) or the PDF viewer chain confirms true positive; note whether traffic is to Graph API/OneDrive (MISTPEN) vs the raw IPs/domains (ForestTiger). 2) Contain: block all three domains and both IPs at proxy/firewall/DNS, isolate the beaconing host, and revoke the user's tokens. 3) Hunt: enumerate every host that resolved/connected to these IOCs in the last 60 days, then pivot to UC1/UC2/UC3 on each; alert on any inbound phishing from already-compromised partner orgs (Lazarus relayed lures through a breached France-based org).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("envell.xyz","enveil.online","uxtramine.org")
    or RemoteIP in ("135.181.67.203","135.181.185.158")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any ("envell.xyz","enveil.online","uxtramine.org")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-68820", "CVE-2025-49113")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-68820", "CVE-2025-49113")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
